description: Compute the customer-acquisition-cost (CAC) payback period per signup cohort and acquisition channel for the subscription service. A cohort is (UTC signup month, channel). acquisition_spend is the channel's spend in the cohort month (0 when there is no spend row). cac = acquisition_spend / cohort_size. Gross margin is 50% of successful payment amounts. For each cohort build the cumulative gross margin by month_offset (0 = signup month) through the latest month with any payment in the dataset, carrying the cumulative value across months without payments. payback_month_offset is the smallest offset at which cumulative gross margin >= acquisition_spend; NULL if not reached within the observed months. Output columns: cohort_month (DATE), channel (STRING), cohort_size (INT64), acquisition_spend (FLOAT64), cac (FLOAT64, 2 decimals), payback_month_offset (INT64). Sort by cohort_month, channel.

channel.description: Acquisition channel; organic has no rows

edge_cases: January paid_search: cumulative margin is 15, 35, 60 at offsets 0, 1, 2, so payback is reached at offset 2
Organic cohort has no spend row: spend 0 and payback at offset 0 even though its first payment is in offset 1
February paid_search cohort does not reach payback in the observed window (NULL), and the failed 500 payment must not count
Spend must be joined once per cohort, not once per user or per payment
common_failure_modes: FM1: Joining channel_spend at user or payment grain multiplies spend (and CAC) by cohort size or payment count
FM3: Comparing cumulative REVENUE (not 50% margin) with spend reports payback one month too early (offset 1)
FM2: Cumulative sum over only the offsets that contain payments skips empty months and can report the wrong payback offset; MIN over an empty set must stay NULL rather than default to 0
